tajweed.readingNote: These describe the recitation of Hafs an Asim, the reading in most printed mushafs. Other authentic readings differ in some durations and details.
tajweed.izhar: The noon is pronounced clearly, with no nasalisation, when one of the six throat letters follows.
tajweed.idgham: The noon merges into the following letter. With ya, noon, meem and waw it is merged with nasalisation; with lam and ra, without.
tajweed.iqlab: The noon becomes a meem before ba, pronounced with nasalisation and the lips together.
tajweed.ikhfa: The noon is hidden - neither clear nor fully merged - and held with nasalisation for about two counts.
tajweed.idghamShafawi: A meem sakinah followed by another meem merges into it, held with nasalisation.
tajweed.ikhfaShafawi: A meem sakinah before ba is hidden at the lips and held with nasalisation.
tajweed.izharShafawi: A meem sakinah before any letter other than meem or ba is pronounced clearly.
tajweed.maddAsli: The natural lengthening of alif, waw and ya - held for two counts, with nothing extending it further.
tajweed.maddMuttasil: A madd letter followed by a hamza in the same word. Held four or five counts, and obligatory.
tajweed.maddMunfasil: A madd letter at the end of a word followed by a hamza at the start of the next. Held four or five counts.
tajweed.maddLazim: A madd letter followed by a sukoon or a doubled letter. Held six counts.
tajweed.qalqalah: An echoing bounce on these five letters when they carry a sukoon. Strongest at the end of a verse.
tajweed.ghunnah: A nasal sound held for about two counts on a doubled noon or meem.
tajweed.lamShamsiyyah: The lam of "al-" is not pronounced; the following letter is doubled instead.
tajweed.lamQamariyyah: The lam of "al-" is pronounced clearly before the fourteen moon letters.

dua.sourceNote: Every dua here is from the Qur'an or from Sahih al-Bukhari, Sahih Muslim or Abu Dawud, and shows its reference so you can check it. The Arabic is the supplication; the transliteration helps you say it and the meaning explains it.
dua.wakingMeaning: All praise is for Allah, who gave us life after He caused us to die, and to Him is the return.
dua.sleepingMeaning: In Your name, O Allah, I die and I live.
dua.leavingHomeMeaning: In the name of Allah, I place my trust in Allah, and there is no power nor strength except with Allah.
dua.enteringMasjidMeaning: O Allah, open for me the doors of Your mercy.
dua.leavingMasjidMeaning: O Allah, I ask You from Your bounty.
dua.afterAdhanMeaning: O Allah, Lord of this perfect call and the prayer to be established, grant Muhammad the intercession and favour.
dua.afterPrayerTasbihMeaning: Glory be to Allah, all praise is for Allah, and Allah is the greatest — each said thirty-three times.
dua.istighfarMeaning: I seek the forgiveness of Allah.
dua.afterEatingMeaning: All praise is for Allah, who fed me this and provided it for me without any might or power on my part.
dua.travelMeaning: Glory to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could never have accomplished it ourselves; and indeed to our Lord we will return.
dua.distressMeaning: There is no god but Allah, the Mighty, the Forbearing; there is no god but Allah, Lord of the mighty throne.
dua.anxietyMeaning: Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best disposer of affairs.
dua.illnessMeaning: O Allah, Lord of mankind, remove the harm and cure — You are the Healer.
dua.morningEveningMeaning: In the name of Allah, with whose name nothing on earth or in heaven can cause harm, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
dua.sayyidulIstighfar: The best way of seeking forgiveness
dua.sayyidulIstighfarMeaning: O Allah, You are my Lord, there is no god but You. You created me and I am Your servant, and I keep to Your covenant and promise as much as I am able.
dua.refugeMeaning: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created.
dua.arabicOnlyNotice: Meanings have been written in English so far. In other languages the Arabic is shown on its own rather than an unchecked translation.

about.title: About the Program
about.programBody1: Islamic knowledge is an important part of every Muslim’s life. Learning and understanding the Qur’an and authentic Sunnah helps us strengthen our faith, improve our worship, develop good character, and live our lives according to Islamic guidance.
about.programBody2: The Weekly Class – JDC Tamil Section is designed to provide a simple, structured, and accessible way for individuals and families to learn about Islam. Through regular weekly classes, we aim to help students build a strong foundation in Islamic knowledge and continue learning at every stage of life.
about.programBody3: Our lessons will be based on the Qur’an and authentic Sunnah and presented in a clear, practical, and easy-to-understand way. We encourage students not only to gain knowledge but also to understand it, benefit from it, and apply it in their daily lives.
about.visionBody: To make authentic Islamic knowledge accessible, meaningful, and beneficial to everyone in our community through a structured and engaging weekly learning program.
about.mission1: Provide authentic Islamic knowledge based on the Qur’an and Sunnah.
about.mission2: Help beginners and continuing students build a strong foundation in Islamic knowledge.
about.mission3: Make Islamic learning simple, clear, practical, and accessible.
about.mission4: Develop understanding in important areas such as Aqeedah, Qur’an, Tafsir, Hadith, Fiqh, Seerah, and Islamic manners and character.
about.mission5: Encourage students to put their knowledge into practice in their daily lives.
about.mission6: Create learning opportunities for children, teenagers, adults, and families.
about.mission7: Provide both in-person and online learning opportunities.
about.mission8: Encourage continuous learning through weekly lessons, activities, revision, quizzes, and assessments.
about.mission9: Create a welcoming learning environment where students can learn, ask questions, and grow in their understanding of Islam.
about.commitmentBody1: We believe that Islamic learning is a lifelong journey. Through the Weekly Class – JDC Tamil Section, we hope to make that journey easier, more engaging, and beneficial for everyone.
about.commitmentBody2: Our goal is not simply to teach lessons, but to inspire a love for knowledge, strengthen faith, and encourage positive change in our daily lives.

qibla.noCompass: This device has no compass, so the dial cannot turn with you. The bearing above is exact — read it against a compass, including the one in your phone's compass app.
qibla.magneticNote: The compass follows magnetic north and can be pulled off by metal, magnets or a phone case. Check it against a second compass before you rely on it.
qibla.problem_denied_body: The qibla is worked out from where you are, so this needs your location. Tap the padlock in the address bar, set Location to Allow, then try again.
qibla.problem_unavailable_body: The device could not fix a position. Indoors and underground are the usual reasons — try again near a window or outside.
qibla.problem_unsupported_body: This browser cannot report a location, so the qibla cannot be worked out. Opening the app on a phone will do it.
